body.heading: Start your diary
paragraphs: On a clear evening, go outside with your adult and find the Moon. Draw a circle in your notebook and shade in the part that looks dark.
Write the date next to your drawing. Your adult can help you write what the shape reminds you of, like a banana, a smile, or a ball.

body.heading: Watch it change
paragraphs: Look again after two or three nights and draw the Moon again. The bright part will look bigger or smaller than before.
The Moon does not really change shape. The Sun lights up different parts of it as it travels around the Earth, so we see a different piece each night.

body.heading: Keep going
paragraphs: After about a month, the shapes repeat. Flick through your diary pages quickly and watch the Moon grow and shrink like a little film.
Cloudy nights are fine to write down too. Scientists write down what they could not see, as well as what they could.

description: For ages 6–9 with an adult: draw the Moon on different nights and watch its shape change.

safetyNotes: Stay with your adult outside and choose a safe spot away from roads and traffic.
It is safe to look at the Moon, but never look directly at the Sun.
screenFreeExtension: Tell a bedtime story about the Moon shape you liked best, or draw tonight's Moon on a card for your wall.
takeaway: The Moon's shape in the sky changes slowly, and drawing it helps you notice.
